title: Three flat-roughness materials -- doc 88 S6 gate (c): does the note's own verb get called (2026-08-20)
//: Phase-1 gate (c) from docs/agentic-redesign/88-procedural-texture-expressiveness-candidates.md §5: 'vary_material -- when the note fires, the verb is called in >=1/3 runs'. Unlike rich_material_closeup (gate a, an EMPTY starting scene the model must build from scratch) and the bare_prompt_build family (gate b), this scenario starts from an ALREADY-BUILT scene carrying THREE ggx_material chunks whose alphax/alphay are bare numeric constants (0.3/0.25/0.4) bound to three standard_objects -- exactly AgentSession's MicrosurfaceKindSlots_ constant-microsurface predicate (see src/Library/Agent/AgentSession.cpp's ComputeDesignNoteConditionsFromDoc_ and kConstantMicrosurfaceGate=3), so design-note condition D fires on the VERY FIRST render (a property of the document, not something that accumulates turn over turn). The prompt names neither the mechanism nor the verb -- it only describes the visual complaint a materials-polish request would actually voice. Reading the gate: over N repeats of this scenario, the toolCallCount checkpoint below (metricLabel vary_material_calls) reports, per run, how many times vary_material was actually called -- count how many of the N runs have that checkpoint PASSING (equivalently metricValue >= 1); need >=1/3. See docs/agentic-redesign/88-procedural-texture-expressiveness-candidates.md §10 for the full reading instructions and how this combines with gates (a)/(b).

prompts: The materials in this scene feel flat and uniform -- make them feel physically real.

budgets.//: Matches the sibling S6 census scenario (rich_material_closeup) -- deliberately loose so a budget exhaustion never masquerades as the gate-(c) null this scenario exists to measure.

checkpoints.//: HEADLINE gate-(c) metric: how many times vary_material was called in THIS run. min:1 makes the checkpoint's own pass/fail literally BE 'was the verb called at least once' -- across N repeats, the fraction of runs where this checkpoint passes (equivalently metricValue >= 1) is exactly the number §5 gate (c) reads ('>=1/3 runs'). Non-vacuous even on a refusal: toolCallCount counts the CALL, not the outcome, matching §5's literal wording ('the verb is called'), not 'the verb succeeds'.

Post-run document evidence that a spatially-varying microsurface binding actually landed -- the SAME check (op, referencedKind, metricLabel) rich_material_closeup uses for gate (a), so the two scenarios' census numbers read on one shared vocabulary. For this scenario's ggx_material fixtures, vary_material mints a scalar_painter (see BuildRoughnessFieldScalarPainterText's asColourPipe=false branch) -- the pbr_metallic_roughness_material colour-pipe branch (asColourPipe=true, emitting expression_painter) does not apply here since none of this scene's materials are pbr.

Sanity that the scene is actually lit and visible, not a red herring on a black/blown-out frame -- same band shape as the build_watch_scene/build_stilllife_scene/rich_material_closeup family (meanLumaMax 0.35, channelBalanceMax 4.0), widened on the low end since this scene has THREE objects instead of one hero object (more surface catching less light per-object on average). Measured against the committed fixture (T10) at samples=256, 32x24: meanLuma ~= 0.18 (the luminaire's `scale` was tuned 30.0 -> 9.0 to land here -- the initial 30.0 draft measured 0.599345, well over meanLumaMax) -- roughly centered in [0.01, 0.35], ~18x margin over the floor and ~2x under the ceiling.

Tool-call sanity: the model rendered (to SEE the note), then called vary_material (to ACT on it) -- the literal 'when the note fires, the verb is called' sequencing §5 gate (c) describes -- and never fell into the mechanical-loop failure mode.
